target.title: fix(android): Talk voice fails when gateway allows local TTS fallback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Android Talk users could lose spoken replies instead of falling back to local TTS when the gateway reports that a `talk.speak` error is fallback-eligible.

Gateway `talk.speak` errors can include `details.fallbackEligible`, but Android previously only looked at a local reason allowlist. That meant a server response such as `reason: "synthesis_failed"` with `fallbackEligible: true` could still be treated as a hard failure on Android.

## Why This Change Was Made

Android now preserves the gateway `details.fallbackEligible` field when parsing RPC errors, and `TalkSpeakClient` uses that server-provided decision before falling back to the legacy reason allowlist. The existing reason-based fallback remains in place for older gateway responses that do not include the field.

The Android native i18n inventory is also refreshed for the source line shift introduced by the gateway details model change.

## User Impact

Android Talk can fall back to device-local TTS when the gateway explicitly marks a remote `talk.speak` failure as eligible, instead of leaving the user without spoken output. Errors that the gateway marks as ineligible still remain visible as failures.

## Evidence

- Added focused Android unit coverage for a `synthesis_failed` gateway error with `fallbackEligible = true`, expecting `TalkSpeakResult.FallbackToLocal`.
- Full Play-flavor Android unit suite passed after syncing with current `origin/main`:

  ```text
  > Task :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest
  BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 3m 29s
  33 actionable tasks: 19 executed, 14 up-to-date
  ```

- `pnpm native:i18n:check` passed after refreshing the native Android i18n inventory.

  ```text
  native-app-i18n: entries=2590 changed=false
  ```

- Source invariant validation also passed:

  ```text
  android talk.speak fallbackEligible source invariants verified
  ```
